title: na4h: tests — whitelist bypass, IPv4-mapped normalization, invalid CIDR
description:
## What
Tests for the peer whitelist feature. Written independently of the implementation — derive expected values from the ipnet spec and RFC 4291 (IPv6 addressing).

## Test cases

### Config parsing tests (add to config.rs mod tests or a new test file)

T1: valid_cidr_parses_ok
  Oracle: ipnet FromStr accepts "10.0.0.0/8" — fact from ipnet docs
  Setup: deserialize TOML with peer_whitelist = ["10.0.0.0/8", "2001:db8::/32"]
  Assert: peer_whitelist.len() == 2; no error

T2: invalid_cidr_fails_deserialization
  Oracle: "not_a_cidr" is not a valid CIDR — trivially true
  Setup: attempt to deserialize TOML with peer_whitelist = ["not_a_cidr"]
  Assert: deserialization returns Err

T3: empty_whitelist_is_default
  Oracle: #[serde(default)] on Vec<T> produces empty vec
  Setup: deserialize TOML without peer_whitelist key
  Assert: peer_whitelist.is_empty()

### Whitelist logic tests (add to session.rs mod tests or smtp integration test)

T4: whitelisted_ip_sets_flag
  Oracle: 192.168.1.50 is contained in 192.168.0.0/16 — per RFC 1918 + ipnet contains semantics
  Setup: config with peer_whitelist = ["192.168.0.0/16"]; peer_addr = "192.168.1.50:12345"
  Assert: connection_whitelisted == true

T5: non_whitelisted_ip_does_not_set_flag
  Oracle: 10.0.0.1 is NOT in 192.168.0.0/16
  Setup: config with peer_whitelist = ["192.168.0.0/16"]; peer_addr = "10.0.0.1:12345"
  Assert: connection_whitelisted == false

T6: empty_whitelist_never_matches
  Oracle: no CIDRs → no matches
  Setup: config with peer_whitelist = []; any peer_addr
  Assert: connection_whitelisted == false

T7: ipv4_mapped_ipv6_matches_ipv4_cidr
  Oracle: RFC 4291 §2.5.5.2 — ::ffff:192.168.1.50 is the IPv4-mapped form of 192.168.1.50
  Setup: config with peer_whitelist = ["192.168.0.0/16"]; peer_addr = "[::ffff:192.168.1.50]:12345"
  Assert: connection_whitelisted == true (after normalization)
  This is the critical regression test for the IPv4-mapped bug.

T8: ipv6_cidr_matches_ipv6_addr
  Oracle: fd00::1 is in fd00::/8 — per ipnet contains semantics
  Setup: config with peer_whitelist = ["fd00::/8"]; peer_addr = "[fd00::1]:12345"
  Assert: connection_whitelisted == true

## Defensive rules
- T7 is the most important test — it catches the IPv4-mapped silent failure
- Do NOT use the whitelist check code as the oracle for any test — use ipnet docs and RFC 4291 as oracles
- Tests must be unit tests (no TCP connection needed) — extract the normalization + check logic into a testable helper function if needed
